target_customer: Container shippers and cargo owners buying ocean transport on short sea routes
problem: Diesel container ships carry high fuel cost and emissions (the launch post cites shipping at 2.2 percent of world CO2).
business_model: Operating shipping lines with owned electric vessels; sales contracts with shippers
product_category: Electric cargo ships and shipping line

founders.name: Prosser Cathey
education: MIT, graduated in three years, multiple majors
Fulbright study of the auto industry transition to EVs
previous_startups: Team previously started two shipping lines (YC page)

competitors.name: Fleetzero
competitors.what: Battery electric ships using modular propulsion and hull construction
competitors.funding_then: Not stated; a 43M Series A came in January 2026

technical_complexity.rationale: Building battery and solar powered cargo vessels needs naval architecture, large battery systems, class approval and shipyard capacity beyond a small software style team.

defensibility.rationale: Patented battery and solar stack spun out of MIT Ocean Engineering per YC page, but vessels are capital intensive and copyable by well funded builders.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented; battery suppliers sell components rather than operate competing lines.

market_need_then: Launch post cites zero emission regulation pressure, fuel as a major operating cost and Department of Energy grants supporting the tech stack.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, benefit focused on reliability, speed and price

rebrands.why: A CB Insights profile says formerly Vault Protocol; single aggregator, no date or reason.

brand_strength.rationale: Name suggests electricity and fits the product, but name is shared with other firms and no brand press was found.

pivots.from: Electric cargo ships described as 3x more profitable than existing ships
pivots.to: Shipping line using smaller vessels with direct service and diesel backup
pivots.why: Not stated; website now stresses a traditional diesel system as backup.

outcome_analysis: Voltic is active, claims over 100M dollars in sales contracts and targets first commercial deployment in early 2026, a self reported figure. Its website now describes a shipping line with diesel backup rather than a pure electric ship. Funding is only supported by aggregators, so capital strength and delivery risk are unverified.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights and VCBacked list about 500K over 2 rounds (YC convertible note, September 2022, and an option or warrant of 20K in April 2025); aggregator only, so no round recorded. Largest maritime VC investor is unnamed. YC page says 4x more profitable while the launch post says 3x. Fleetzero was founded in 2021 per YesPress but I found no source dated near the batch; source_date is null. A May 2026 podcast features Voltic's chief commercial officer, which suggests activity.
